activity: Picnic in Brockwell Park — bread, cheese, fruit, a blanket, no screens.
Start a jigsaw puzzle together, worked on over an evening or two.
Home cinema night — blackout the room, snacks, a film you've been meaning to watch.
Wander a farmers market or car boot sale — no list, just browse and taste.
Try making a cocktail you've never had, and make a mess of the kitchen.
Photo walk, phones only — pick a loose theme and take ten shots each.
Cafe crawl — two or three new coffee shops, a small something at each.
Stargazing somewhere dark — drive out past the streetlights with a blanket.
Learn a short dance together from a beginner tutorial, even badly.
Book a one-off craft class — pottery, candle-making, whatever's on.
Scenic drive, no destination — pick a direction and stop somewhere.
Cook a big meal and invite someone over — plan a menu and host.
Card game marathon — play until one of you hits a target score.
Browse a bookshop, pick something for each other, read on a bench outside.
Eat a cuisine neither of you has tried, with no expectations.
A small garden or balcony project — pots, herbs, hands in the dirt.
Karaoke at home — find a playlist, take turns, no judgment.
Free self-guided walking tour of somewhere near you you've never explored.
Bake something from scratch together — bread, a cake, fiddly steps.
A do-nothing afternoon — same room, same blanket, no agenda.
Mini golf or an arcade — low-stakes, loser buys next round.
Wander Brockwell Park's walled garden — roses and ponds, five minutes from the station.
Visit the volunteer-run Brockwell Park greenhouses and walled orchard, Thu-Sun.
Browse Herne Hill Market — a Sunday market on Railton Road, 50+ stalls.
Visit Dulwich Picture Gallery, England's first public art gallery — Tue-Sun.
Hire a boat on Dulwich Park's lake, then wander its paths and hidden ponds.
Follow the Dulwich Street Art Walk, including the mosaic-covered House of Dreams.
Explore the free Horniman Museum — anthropology, aquarium, butterfly house.
Picnic in the Horniman's gardens, sixteen acres with some of south London's best views.
Walk the restored Victorian dinosaur trail at Crystal Palace Park, free anytime.
Get lost in the Crystal Palace Park hedge maze, with a skatepark nearby.
Browse the Crystal Palace Flea — 30+ vintage and homeware traders in the park's Bowl.
West Norwood Feast — 100+ street food stalls, first Sunday of the month.
Wander West Norwood Cemetery, one of London's grand, overgrown 'Magnificent Seven'.
Food crawl through Brixton Village and Market Row — two or three small plates each.
Catch a film at a south London picture house.
Street food and live music in Hootananny's Brixton pub garden.
Rooftop Cinema Club on the Bussey Building roof in Peckham, summer screenings.
Cocktails at the Bussey rooftop bar, 360-degree views over Peckham.
Walk Streatham Common and the walled Rookery garden with its waterfall.
Explore Peckham Levels, a car park turned food hall, studios and bars.
Walk Sydenham Hill Wood, the old Great North Wood's largest fragment, near the Horniman.

Explore Dacres Wood, a small, little-known nature reserve near the Horniman.
Catch Smithfield Market at dawn — 800 years old, stalls pack up by 7am.
Catch a show at the Barbican — theatre, concerts, and a tropical conservatory.
Browse Leather Lane Market for food, coffee and handmade goods by Farringdon.
Find the memorial wall at Postman's Park — 54 Victorian plaques, a quiet detour.
Walk the 'Wobbly Bridge' between St Paul's and Tate Modern for a skyline view.
Explore Tate Modern, free entry, with a top-floor terrace over the Thames.
Shop and eat at Coal Drops Yard, a converted coal depot by King's Cross.
Walk the Regent's Canal from Granary Square toward Camden or Primrose Hill.
Catch an immersive show at Lightroom, King's Cross — check what's currently on.
See a free exhibition at the British Library, steps from St Pancras.
Tour Camden Town Brewery near Kentish Town West — tours and tastings.
Visit Kentish Town City Farm, a small, surprisingly quiet city farm.
Visit the Freud Museum, Sigmund Freud's preserved final home in West Hampstead.
West Hampstead's Saturday farmers' market, by the Thameslink station.
Explore Verulamium Park's Roman ruins, 20 minutes direct from Herne Hill.
Visit St Albans Cathedral, free entry, with 13th-century wall paintings.
Browse St Albans market, named Britain's best large outdoor market in 2024.
Pint at Ye Olde Fighting Cocks, reputedly one of England's oldest pubs.
Walk the Parkland Walk, a disused railway from Finsbury Park to Alexandra Palace.
Day trip to walk Brighton beach — about an hour direct, pebbles past the pier.
Catch a free contemporary art show at the South London Gallery in Peckham.
Visit the Garden Museum, a deconsecrated church by Lambeth Palace telling garden history.
Explore Black British history at the Black Cultural Archives on Windrush Square.
Take a guided tour of the Cinema Museum, housed in Charlie Chaplin's old workhouse.
Explore the free Imperial War Museum on Lambeth Road.
Explore the British Museum's world collections, free entry, in Bloomsbury.
See Old Masters at the free National Gallery on Trafalgar Square.
Wander Tate Britain's five centuries of British art on Millbank, free entry.
Explore the V&A's design and decorative arts collection in South Kensington.
See the blue whale and dinosaur skeletons at the Natural History Museum.
Explore interactive galleries at the Science Museum in South Kensington, free entry.
Get lost in Sir John Soane's eccentric, crammed house-museum near Holborn.
See armour and Old Masters for free at the Wallace Collection near Oxford Street.
Browse centuries of British faces at the National Portrait Gallery, Trafalgar Square.
Explore product and fashion design at the Design Museum in Kensington.
